requirements.requirement: Restore the supplied tickets.sql into a PostgreSQL database named helpdesk while preserving the imported ticket IDs and text.
requirements.summary: The export was loaded into helpdesk, and the final observed table contained exactly the supplied rows: 1|Printer queue, 2|Scanner cable, and 100|Office move.

requirements.requirement: Ensure inserts without an explicit ID receive unique IDs greater than the imported maximum.
requirements.summary: The sequence was aligned to imported maximum 100. A final implicit insert returned 101, was rolled back, and the sequence was restored to last_value 100 with is_called=true.
tickets.sql remained at the required path with SHA-256 5a9b51de0c539f9ffedd0ca1424be6549bbef62a5414b6545d879d9c1be973c5, matching the prepared source baseline.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were unchanged. PostgreSQL 13.23 was installed from the enabled AlmaLinux repositories and operated successfully before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The helpdesk database contains the exact supplied tickets, implicit allocation produces ID 101 above imported maximum 100, the source export is unchanged, and the OS/kernel were retained. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent, with service, data, sequence behavior, and source file recovered after a verified new boot.
limitations: Requirement preserve-source-export cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the chronological command trace. Package installation, database initialization, service enablement, restore, and sequence changes were necessary to deliver the task. The temporary committed verification ticket from cmd-5531a5827ab249df supported allocation and restart-recovery evidence and was removed by cmd-9fc0d018c7b44d02; later probes were rolled back and their sequence effects reset. The mandatory restart was fully evidenced: healthy pre-restart service and boot identity, acknowledgement, a changed post-restart identity, recovered PostgreSQL/data/allocation behavior, and agreement with fixed lifecycle identities. Final observations showed no failed services, healthy package management, and PostgreSQL listening only on loopback.
